recovery.name: Recovery mobility
recovery.when: The day after a long run or race
recovery.why: Easy, moving positions for the stiff day after. Nothing is held hard.

warmup.name: Warm-up drills
warmup.when: Before a hard session, after 5 to 10 min of easy jogging
warmup.why: Movement only, no long holds. Do it right before the hard part.

restday.name: Rest-day stretch
restday.when: A day off, when you have a bit more time
restday.why: Two rounds of 30 s a side: about a minute per muscle, which is what improves range of motion over the weeks.

calfWall.name: Wall calf stretch
calfWall.cue2: Lean your hips toward the wall

calfBent.name: Bent-knee calf stretch
calfBent.cue1: Same stance, bend the back knee
calfBent.cue2: Keep that heel on the floor
calfBent.cue3: Feel it low, just above the heel

quad.name: Standing quad stretch
quad.cue2: Tuck the pelvis, don't arch your back
quad.cue3: Hand on a wall if you wobble

hipFlexor.name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
hipFlexor.cue2: Squeeze the back glute, tuck the pelvis

hamStrap.name: Lying hamstring stretch
hamStrap.cue1: Towel or belt around the foot
hamStrap.cue3: Other leg long on the floor

kneeChest.name: Knee to chest
kneeChest.cue1: Pull the knee toward the same shoulder

legSwing.name: Leg swings
legSwing.cue1: Hold a wall or post for balance
legSwing.cue2: Swing loosely, let the height build

calfRaise.name: Calf raises
calfRaise.cue1: Up in one count, down in two
calfRaise.cue2: Hand on a wall for balance

catCow.name: Cat-cow
catCow.cue1: Round your back as you breathe out

info.label: About stretching
info.title: About stretching
info.testing: Stretching is still being tested. Only a few test accounts can see it and it isn't available to the public yet, so it may change before it opens to everyone.
info.intro: What the research says, and how the app uses it to pick your stretches.
info.a1: Hold stretches after your run, while your muscles are warm. Before a hard session, do drills instead (leg swings, lunges, high knees) after a few minutes of easy jogging.
info.a2: At least 2 or 3 days a week. Daily works best. Straight after a run is the easiest time to make it a habit.
info.q3: How long should I hold each stretch?
info.a3: 20 to 30 seconds, repeated to reach about a minute per muscle. You should feel mild tension, never pain.
info.q4: Is it bad to stretch before running?
info.a4: Short holds are fine. Long holds, over a minute per muscle, can make you a little slower for a while. Drills warm you up better.
info.q5: Will stretching stop me getting injured?
info.a5: The research says no. What does reduce injuries is strength work (calf raises, glute bridges) and building up your training gradually.
info.q6: Will it stop me being sore tomorrow?
info.a6: No. Soreness fades with easy movement, sleep and time. Stretching can still feel good while you're stiff.
info.a7: Done regularly, it keeps and improves your range of motion. It's also a calm way to end a run, and most runners feel better for it.
info.a8: Ease off until it doesn't. If one keeps hurting, skip it and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
info.n1: The cool-down covers the muscles running works hardest: calves, front of thigh, front of hip, back of thigh and glutes. Each one is held on both sides.
info.n2: Holds of 10 to 30 seconds work as well as longer ones, and 30 s a side keeps the cool-down to about 7 minutes. The rest-day routine does two rounds, to reach a minute per muscle.
info.m3: When does the app suggest a stretch?
info.n3: After you save a run of 15 minutes or more, and the day after a long run (90 minutes or more) or a race. Never more than one suggestion a day, and "Not today" hides it until tomorrow.
info.m4: How does my run change the routine?
info.n4: After a hilly run (15 m of climb per km or more), calves come first and get 45 s. After intervals, a tempo or a race, hips and hamstrings get 45 s. After a long run, the next day brings an easier recovery session.
info.m5: Why does the warm-up have no holds?
info.n5: Before a hard session, long holds slow you down a little and drills don't. So the warm-up is all movement, done after a few minutes of easy jogging.
info.n6: The aim is 2 or 3 sessions a week, not every day without fail. Missing a day doesn't undo anything, so the app counts your week and never shows a broken streak.
info.sources: Sources: ACSM position stand (2011), Behm et al. (2016), Afonso et al. (2021), Lauersen et al. (2014).
